overview: Orange Pi boards are the most common Raspberry Pi alternative: similar credit-card size, a similar 40-pin header, often more RAM or a faster SoC for less money — but a much less consistent experience. 'Orange Pi' isn't one board but a whole family from different SoC vendors (Allwinner, Rockchip, and others), so tutorials, GPIO pin functions, and OS image quality vary noticeably between models in a way they simply don't across the tightly-controlled Raspberry Pi lineup. It's a reasonable choice when a project's budget or RAM requirements rule out a Pi, as long as you're prepared to do more of your own troubleshooting.
simpleSummary: A Raspberry-Pi-like mini computer, often cheaper or faster but less consistent to use.

specifications.processor: Varies by model (commonly Allwinner or Rockchip, quad-core Cortex-A53, ~1.8 GHz)
specifications.connectivity: Gigabit Ethernet; WiFi/Bluetooth on some models only
specifications.gpio: 40-pin header, Raspberry-Pi-like layout (pin functions vary by model — verify against that specific board's documentation)

pinMap.name: I2C SDA
pinMap.function: I2C data line — physical position generally matches Pi layout, but always confirm against the specific model's pinout diagram.
pinMap.gotcha: The single biggest Orange Pi gotcha: assuming a Raspberry Pi pinout diagram applies exactly. It often doesn't.

useCases.title: Home media server / NAS
